topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: A front-end sales load is paid out of the amount of money you have to purchase mutual fund shares. Thus, it decreases the amount of money you have to invest. However, the fee will be paid out of the money you receive when you exit the fund.
answer: A sales load is a fee mutual funds typically use to compensate brokers who sell their shares. A front-end sales load is charged when you purchase shares, reducing the money available to buy them. A back-end (deferred) sales load is charged when you redeem, or sell back, your shares, reducing the money you receive. In short: front-end means a charge at purchase; back-end means a charge at redemption. The prospectus explains how a fund calculates its sales load.
